sources.title: Ohio State University — Jesse Owens biography

discipline.rationale: Sustained a rigorous multi-event training regimen under coach Larry Snyder at Ohio State while also working part-time jobs to support himself, since he was not offered the same athletic scholarship support as white contemporaries — a real, documented pattern of sustained effort.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Set or tied six world records in under an hour at the 1935 Big Ten Championships (a specific, officially documented competitive result, not an anecdote), and his long-jump record stood for 25 years — real, sustained excellence across events.

persistence.rationale: Continued training and competing at the elite level through documented segregation-era hardships (including being required to use separate travel and lodging from white teammates at some meets) without disengaging from competition.

achievement_drive.rationale: Trained and competed simultaneously across multiple distinct events (100m, 200m, long jump, relay) at a world-class level, evidencing sustained multi-event goal pursuit rather than success in a single narrow specialty.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Competed across several track and field events, but these remain within one broad sport rather than genuinely unrelated domains — scored moderately rather than assumed high, since 'cross-domain' here is really 'multi-event within athletics.'

competitiveness.rationale: The 1935 Big Ten Championships performance (six records/ties in roughly 45 minutes) is a specific, officially documented competitive result reflecting real, sustained competitive drive under pressure.

proactive_agency.rationale: Took on an extended post-competition career as a public speaker and goodwill ambassador, a real but only moderately corroborated pattern of self-directed activity beyond his athletic career.

resourcefulness.rationale: Worked multiple part-time jobs while training at an elite level due to being denied the athletic-scholarship support given to white contemporaries — a real but thinly-documented specific behavioral pattern beyond the general fact of the hardship itself.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Became a public lecture-circuit speaker for decades after retiring from competition — real public engagement, though the surviving record documents the fact of the career more than specific behavioral instances within it.

adaptability.rationale: Transitioned from world-class competitive athlete to public speaker and later business ventures — a real career transition, but with only moderate independent corroboration of the transition's specifics.

provenance.notes: First-batch diversity pick deliberately testing a DIFFERENT thin-evidence case than Sun Tzu: a well-documented MODERN figure whose competitive results are extensively recorded but whose personal behavioral/personality documentation is comparatively thin absent deeper research into his own later writings — exactly the 'evidence availability' diversity dimension the brief asked this batch to exercise. 20th_century, north_america, athletics domain not represented anywhere in the current roster besides Serena Williams/Simone Biles/Bruce Lee, none of whom are historical (mid-20th-century) athletes.
